main_text.head: DE RATIONALI VIRTVTE ORGANICA.
PROPOSITIO I.
main_text.p: Organicas virtutes eas dicimus, quæ occupatur in rectè apparandis Instrumentis, ad disciplinas assequendas à natura nobis attributis.
Duo verò hæc sunt[?], ORATIO & RATIOCINATIO: quibus ut quomodo natura utimur, ita longè tutius & rectius arte. Cicero in lib.Orat.
Quòd si igitur in sola Oratione fuerint occupata; pariunt illa GRAMMATICAM, benè loquendi artificio contentam.
Si verò in sola Ratiocinatione, LOGICAM, nobile instrumentum dextrè philosophandi, & in Philosophia verum à falso distinguendi.
Si autem in utrisq; simul versentur, RHETORICAM, facultatem ornatè copiosèq; dicendi progenerant. Arist.Rhet.1.c.3 Alexand. in Præf. in lib.1. Top.
Et eiusdè[?] insuper colonias tres: ORATORIAM, HISTORICAM, & POETICAM. Quæusus & fructus quidam esse iudicantur Logicarum artium exercendarum.
His igitur Instrumentis Philosophiæ universæ, Theoricæ, Practicæ, sed & superiorū quoq; facultatū, Medicinæ dico, Iurisprudentiæ & S.S.Theologiæ mysteria, initiatis referantur, aperiuntur & patefiunt

page.notes: Drop cap "O" of the first paragraph is joined to "Organicas". "sunt" after "hæc" is partly obscured by a stray ink mark; read as "sunt" with [?]. "eiusdè" is faintly printed and uncertain. "Quæusus" and "ORATORIAM" are read as printed. The word "Gram-" at the foot is the catchword for the next page, not part of the text. Text is continuous from the previous page only in the sense that the page opens a new division; no running head or page number is printed.
